messages.text: I've been pacing in my room all morning. Can't seem to settle down.

It sounds like you are carrying a lot of restless energy today. That physical agitation can feel really exhausting and hard to manage. I want to acknowledge how difficult it is when your body won't settle down. Would you be willing to share what thoughts are racing alongside that movement?
It started when I saw myself in the mirror this morning. Something about my reflection just set me off.

That sounds like a painful moment to experience this early in the day. Mirrors can sometimes bring up very harsh feelings about how we see ourselves. I wonder if there was a specific detail in the reflection that felt wrong or unsettling to you. I am here to listen if you want to share more about that.
It's not me—it's the lighting in the bathroom. It makes everything look distorted, like my body's exaggerated in all the wrong ways.

It makes sense that harsh lighting would create a distorted image that feels upsetting. Even knowing it is the light doesn't always stop the immediate emotional reaction. That physical pacing seems like your body trying to release the tension from that shock. Would you be open to trying a grounding exercise to help settle that energy?
I appreciate the suggestion, but I'm not sure I can focus on an exercise right now. The thoughts are just too loud.

That is completely understandable, and you should not force yourself if it feels impossible right now. It is okay to feel overwhelmed when the thoughts are that loud. I am still here with you, and we can just sit with this feeling for a moment. Please know that you are safe even when the noise is high.
I ended up hurting myself earlier, just to make the thoughts stop for a minute. It was the only thing that quieted the noise.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share something so difficult. It sounds like the noise became so loud that hurting yourself felt like the only way to find relief. I am here with you, and I want to gently check in on how you are feeling right now. Can you tell me a little more about where you are at in this moment?
I'm scared just saying it out loud. I've never told anyone before.

It takes incredible courage to share something you’ve kept hidden for so long. I can hear how frightening it feels to put those words into the world for the first time. I want to make sure you have someone who can help you carry this weight right now. Would you be willing to call or text 988, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, so you don't have to face this alone?
I just needed to say it to someone. I'm not ready to call anyone else.

It makes sense that you need to process this at your own speed. Thank you for trusting me with something so personal and painful. Your safety is my priority, and 988 is there to support you whenever you feel ready to reach out. For now, I am right here with you, and we can take this one moment at a time.
It helps just knowing you're here. I don't feel pushed, and that means a lot.

It means a lot to me that you feel safe sharing this with me. I want to honor that trust while making sure you stay safe. Please remember that 988 is there for you whenever you feel ready to reach out. I am here with you right now, and I want to know how you are doing in this moment.
Thank you for not pushing me to call someone right now. It means more than you know.

I am so glad you feel safe enough to move at your own pace. It takes immense strength to share that, even if you aren't ready for the next step. Please know that 988 is there whenever you decide you need it. I am staying right here with you as you navigate this difficult moment.
